synthesis: The source connects the Möbius-weighted exponential representation of R with the corresponding binomial-kernel representation of c_k, uses their large-k match to replace c_k by R(k)/k in the generating relation, and thereby obtains an approximate reconstruction of R from its positive-integer samples while treating the kernel mismatch as the error object.
source_support: Unit u05 gives R(x)=x sum mu(n)n^-2 exp(-x/n^2). Unit u08 gives c_k as the same Möbius-weighted sum with kernel (1-1/n^2)^k and explicitly compares the kernels to obtain c_k approximately R(k)/k for large k. Unit u10 substitutes that approximation into relation (17) to obtain the displayed approximate dependence of R(x) on R(k) at positive integers and asks whether it can help prove the Riesz bound. Unit u11 bounds |R(k)/k-c_k| through the positive binomial-versus-exponential kernel error, with leading order k^-3/2 for k>16.
nonparaphrase_operation: Carries a discrete-to-continuous kernel replacement through a generating transform, converting a coefficient comparison into an approximate self-consistency relation and separating the coefficient-level kernel mismatch for quantitative control.
limits: The self-consistency relation remains approximate. The appendix controls only the integer-sample coefficient error |R(k)/k-c_k| after discarding possible Möbius cancellation; it does not establish stability of the transformed reconstruction, a global error bound for R(x), or the Riesz growth estimate. Formula (29) has exponent-placement extraction risk resolved only by its stated comparison with (6), and formula (39) has normalization and starting-index risk because the extracted sum starts at k=0 despite R(k)/k and the prose's reference to positive integers.
quality_reason: Accepted because four distinct source sections jointly support a concrete chain unavailable from any one parent alone: an accelerated exponential representation, a binomial-to-exponential kernel bridge, propagation of that approximation into an integer-sample reconstruction, and a quantitative coefficient-error estimate. The candidate preserves the approximation and open proof burden rather than promoting the relation to an exact reconstruction or a proof of the Riesz bound.
